items.title: Joe LaBarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 15, 2021
items.q: My brothers and I grew up listening to all of the cats out here: Art Pepper, Bud Shank, Bill Perkins, you know Teddy Edwards

ctx.x: Can you describe for me, I’m totally fascinated by the life of a studio musician and starting from the phone call, where that comes from be it X studio at this time and how much you know about the music and what is the expectation of the producer and all that stuff. That’s a long question.

It’s a long question and unfortunately you’re asking the wrong guy, Monk, ‘cause I’m not a studio musician. I never have been. I mean I made the mistake early on when we got to town — my wife and I’m, I’m remarried now and we’ve been together now for 26 years and we have a hard and fast rule of a vacation every year. And one year one of the big film composers in Los Angeles put out the call to me for a session, you know, and it goes through a service. So I’m talking to the person at the service, she’s saying so…
Did you play a role in finding your own gigs for the music?
